chunks: Muhammad and others, from Ahmad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Atiyya, from Hisham ibn Ahmad, who said:
Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was saying to Musadif: 'Go early to your honour,' meaning the marketplace.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) mean by calling the market 'your honour'?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) encourages Musadif to proceed to the market, metaphorically referring to it as one's 'izz' (honor or dignity). This reflects the Shia scholarly view that honest trade is not merely a livelihood but a noble pursuit that sustains social independence and reflects the dignity of the believer. The advice underscores the importance of diligence and attentiveness in business as a form of worship and self-sufficiency.

en.hubeali: Muhammad and someone else, from Ahmad Bin Isa, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Atiyya, from Hisham Bin Ahmad who said,
‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> was saying to Musadif: ‘Go early to your honour- meaning the marketplace’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad and others have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ali ibn ‘Atiyyah from Hisham ibn Ahmar who has said the following: “
Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say to Musadif, ‘Proceed toward your honor, meaning thereby place of business, the market place.’”
